## Overview

Lets a streaming-input session run past `max_model_len` on sliding-window RoPE models, behind `--enable-unbounded-streaming-input`. Experimental, off by default. Builds on #45022 (merged, in v0.32.0).

An earlier Voxtral-only version has run in production at LinTO since June. It ran the live captions of Wikimania 2026 on one L40S at `--max-model-len 8192`, where a session would otherwise stop after 11 min: 6 concurrent streams translated into 5 languages, multi-hour sessions, all week. A throughput bench on the same card, without translation, kept up in real time with 17 streams.

## Claims

- A Voxtral realtime session no longer stops at `max_model_len`. Its KV usage stays constant, since the windows already bound it.
- The shift is model-agnostic: each attention layer is rotated with its own RoPE, read from the model at startup. It works for any streaming-input session on a model where every attention layer uses a sliding window and plain, Llama 3 or YaRN RoPE.
- Unsupported models and configurations are refused at startup.
- With the flag off, the new code does not run.

## Validation

RTX 4090, base `4d1376a492`. Test commands, all on CUDA unless marked CPU:

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_reanchor_rotary.py tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py` (CPU) | 64 passed |
| `pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py` (CPU) | 293 passed, 4 failed (`ParallelConfig` validation without GPUs, same on main) |
| `pytest tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py` (CPU) | 117 passed |
| `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_unbounded_streaming.py` (V1, V2) | 3 passed |
| `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error pytest "tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_voxtral_realtime.py::test_voxtral_realtime_reanchor_parity"` (V1, V2) | 1 passed on each |

The e2e test runs Llama-3.2-1B (real weights, Llama 3 RoPE, every layer overridden to a sliding window) with shifts and without, and fails with no rotation, with the wrong sign and with the angle off by one position. Locally the weights come from the public `unsloth` mirror.

Reduced bench on the same model, 60 chunks of 120 tokens plus 8 generated, 14 shifts, against a run without shifts (script not in this PR). A flip changes the later input, so the logprobs are compared up to the first one:

| Runner | dtype | RoPE | First token flip (of 480) | max \|Δlogprob\| up to there |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| V1, V2 (same numbers) | fp32 | Llama 3 | 114 | 0.023 |
| V1, V2 (same numbers) | bf16 | Llama 3 | 124 | 0.20 |
| V2 | fp32 | YaRN | 269 | 0.066 |
| V2 | fp32 | plain | 352 | 0.062 |

For scale, with no shift at all, computing the RoPE table in float64 instead of float32 moves the fp32 logprobs by as much: max 0.017 to 0.047, mean 0.003 to 0.006. With shifts: max 0.032 to 0.052, mean 0.003 to 0.006. Without the rotation: max 2.9, mean 0.93.

| Run | Compared to | Result |
|---|---|---|
| V2, real time | | no gap, 0 errors |
| V1, real time | V2, real time | no gap, 0 errors, identical text (20,370 chars) |
| V2, same audio fed faster than real time | no shifts (`max_model_len` 32768) | identical for 10,188 tokens (815 s), then a near tie flips; 98.25 % of 18,760 tokens the same |
| V1, same | V2, same | identical tokens |
| V2, real time | previous Voxtral-only code | identical for 11,482 chars, then a near tie flips; 99.57 % word similarity |

The run without shifts is fed faster than real time because it falls behind on this GPU after about 20 min (#58324).

Shifts flip near ties, so the transcript drifts from a run without shifts by 1.75 % of tokens. The largest difference is a stretch without punctuation of 77 s at one place in the audio. It is not caused by the shifts. Same audio, 10 sessions starting 165 to 210 s before that place:

| | Sessions with a stretch of 30 s or more there | Of which 77 s |
|---|---|---|
| No shift | 7 of 10 | 1 |
| 35 shifts in total | 7 of 10, the same 7 | 1, the same |

Across these 10 sessions, 99.63 % of the tokens are the same with and without shifts.

CI: the e2e test runs on PRs (`e2e-core-1-gpu`), the rotary and scheduler tests in `v1-executor-worker`, the Voxtral parity test in the nightly multimodal step.
```
--enable-unbounded-streaming-input --disable-prefix-caching
```

## Details

### Who needs it today: Voxtral realtime

A Voxtral session stops at `max_model_len`: about 2 h 55 at the default, 11 min at `--max-model-len 8192`. The client has to reconnect and the model loses its context. The vLLM recipe for this model tells users to restart long sessions periodically.

On a sliding-window model the KV of a streaming session is already bounded by the window. What stops the session is the position counter reaching `max_model_len`. The [technical report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11298) says Voxtral's sliding windows support "arbitrarily long streams with bounded memory".

### How it works

RoPE scores only depend on `m - n`, and a query only sees keys in `(m-W, m]`, so shifting every live position down by `d` keeps the scores the same apart from rounding. When a session resumes on a new input chunk close to the cap, the scheduler drops its head (blocks already evicted by the window, mm features, token ids) and the worker re-rotates the cached keys in place by `R(-d)`.

The margin before the cap defaults to half of `max_model_len - W` and can be set with `--unbounded-streaming-input-margin-tokens`. With `d >= W` a key is rotated at most once before it leaves the window, so rounding does not build up.

The position scale of a block-pooled layer comes from its `tokens_per_state`. The only model-side change is in Voxtral: its audio buffer no longer ends the stream at `max_model_len` when the flag is on. `buffer_realtime_audio` gains that keyword, and it is only passed when the flag is on, so models outside this repo are not affected.

Where to look: `vllm/v1/core/sched/reanchor.py` (what a shift does to a session) and `vllm/v1/worker/reanchor_rotary.py` (startup checks and the rotation). The core files only get the hooks. 456 added lines without config, tests and docs, 329 of them in these two new files.

Rounding: cos and sin are computed in fp32 and the keys rounded back to their dtype, so in bf16 the error is per element and not the same for all keys of a frequency. On a shift step each layer does one GPU copy and rotate; steady state does not change. A large `max_model_len` costs CPU, every token resends the session since the last shift.

Why V1 as well as V2: our production still runs on V1. Both runners call the same function, so it costs one hook and the init check.

### Refused at startup

Non-sliding attention, a RoPE other than plain, Llama 3 or YaRN (exact class), a RoPE built for another head size, compressed KV states, quantized KV, KV sharing, prefix caching, KV connectors, KV offloading, encoder cache connectors, speculative decoding, pipeline parallelism, prefill context parallelism, non-CUDA, and a `max_model_len` under the window + the margin + one KV block.

### Limits

- Not detected at startup, needs an override to be used at all: attention that depends on absolute positions outside RoPE (`llama_4_scaling`, Rnj1 chunked attention, Moondream3 `tau_pos`) and RoPE held but unused (Step3p5 NoPE).
- A chunk larger than `max_model_len - W - 1 block` goes past `max_model_len`, as it does on main today (#42502, #51900, #63113 are open).
- If more sessions run than fit in the KV cache, all of them stall (#60137), with or without the flag.
- A turn that generates past the cap is cut there and the next chunk shifts. Voxtral generates 1 token per chunk.
- The API server keeps each session's token ids and text, about 100 MB per session per day (estimated from the code, not measured).
- The docs ask for a text window of 1024 or more: on long read speech a 256 window drops text for minutes, with or without shifts (#47614).

### Not covered: Qwen3-ASR realtime

Qwen3-ASR realtime, the other realtime model in vLLM, is refused at startup: it uses full attention, so nothing ever leaves its KV cache, and M-RoPE. Its sessions grow because earlier segments are carried over. #56218 and #51037 would change that, which may remove the need. If the context stays, three pieces would make it work:

1. Free the old KV blocks of a live session: #53871 (RFC #51948), plus a policy that calls it.
2. Keep the position counter under `max_model_len` without re-prefill: this PR, plus an inverse rotation for M-RoPE (still a constant rotation, the 3 axes move together).
3. Measure quality. The model has no sliding window in its config, and #56218 shows that carried context can hurt it. If the prompt is kept as an attention sink, a shift moves it to a negative position, and shifting only the rest changes its distance to the query ([comment on #51948](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51948#issuecomment-5907011073)). The consolidation in #53876 re-prefills the window from position 0 instead.

Happy to work on this with @nvbfalk.

### Not a duplicate

#53871, #53876 and #43374 free KV of a live session. Here the KV is already bounded and the position counter is what has to move. #42502, #51900 and #63113 end the session or reject the input at the cap; this PR keeps it under the cap.

AI-assisted (Opus 5.5, `Assisted-by` trailers on the commits): most of the migration from the Voxtral-specific code to this model-agnostic version was done that way. Reviewed and validated by me.

+
+### Serving Voxtral realtime
+
+`Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-2602` uses a sliding window in every attention layer,
+in the text decoder and in the audio encoder. The KV cache of a session stops
+growing once both windows are full.
+
+**Windows.** Both are set with `--hf-overrides`:
+
+```bash
+vllm serve mistralai/Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-2602 --tokenizer-mode mistral \
+  --hf-overrides '{"text_config":{"sliding_window":1024},"audio_config":{"sliding_window":256}}'
+```
+
+| Window | Key | Unit | Default |
+| ------ | --- | ---- | ------- |
+| Text (decoder) | `text_config.sliding_window` | token (80 ms of audio) | 8192 (~11 min) |
+| Audio (encoder) | `audio_config.sliding_window` | frame (20 ms of audio) | 750 (15 s) |
+
+Smaller windows use less KV cache per session, so more sessions fit in the same
+memory. A session holds about 32 MiB + 0.125 MiB per text token + 0.25 MiB per
+audio frame: 224 MiB with 1024 and 256, 1.2 GiB with the defaults.
+
+!!! warning
+    Keep the text window at 1024 or more. On long read speech, with a 256 text window
+    the model sometimes output nothing over real speech for minutes
+    ([#47614](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47614)). A 90 min run going
+    from 2 to 8 streams lost 20 min of text this way. It did not happen at 1024.
+    Stretches without punctuation or capitals reached 3 min at 256, 77 s at 1024 with
+    or without shifts, and about 30 s from 2048 up. The audio window (256 or 750) made
+    no difference.
+
+**Session length.** By default, `--max-model-len` caps a session: one text token
+per 80 ms of audio, so about 2 h 55 at 131072 (the default) and 11 min at 8192. At
+the cap, the server ends the session with `transcription.done`. To go on, the client
+sends a new `input_audio_buffer.commit` or reconnects, and the model starts again
+without context.
+
+`--enable-unbounded-streaming-input` (off by default) removes the cap. Before a
+session reaches `--max-model-len`, its positions are shifted down and its cached
+keys are re-rotated to match, so the attention scores stay the same apart from
+rounding. The KV cache of the session stays bounded by the windows.
+
+- Requirements, checked at startup: every attention layer uses a sliding window
+  and RoPE (plain, Llama 3 or YaRN) over its whole key, the KV cache is not
+  quantized, prefix caching is off (`--disable-prefix-caching`), and the platform
+  is CUDA. KV connectors, KV offloading, encoder cache connectors, speculative
+  decoding, pipeline parallelism and prefill context parallelism are refused. Any
+  streaming-input session on such a model works the same way.
+- `--max-model-len` must be at least the text window plus 2 KV cache blocks (256
+  tokens on Voxtral), so `--max-model-len 8192` with the default text window of
+  8192 is refused. It no longer limits the session, and a large value costs CPU:
+  every token resends the session since the last shift. 8192 is enough with a 1024
+  text window.
+- `--unbounded-streaming-input-margin-tokens` (default: half of
+  `max_model_len - text window`): the shift happens this many tokens before
+  `--max-model-len`. The rest of the room is roughly the distance between two
+  shifts: with 8192 and 1024, a shift every 3456 tokens, about 4.5 min.
+- A shift only happens when a new input chunk arrives. A chunk can hold up to
+  `max_model_len - text window - 1 block` input tokens. If it generates more
+  tokens than the margin, the turn ends early with `finish_reason` `length` and
+  the session continues with the next chunk. Voxtral sends and generates one token
+  per chunk, so this only concerns other models.
+
+**16 GiB GPU.** This command starts on an RTX 4090 Laptop (16 GiB):
+
+```bash
+PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True \
+vllm serve mistralai/Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-2602 --tokenizer-mode mistral \
+  --hf-overrides '{"text_config":{"sliding_window":1024},"audio_config":{"sliding_window":256}}' \
+  --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-batched-tokens 512 --max-num-seqs 12 \
+  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.82 --disable-prefix-caching \
+  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"PIECEWISE"}' \
+  --enable-unbounded-streaming-input
+```
+
+CUDA graphs are captured for batches of up to 2 x `--max-num-seqs` tokens, so keep
+`--max-num-seqs` close to the number of sessions you need. `expandable_segments`
+reduces memory fragmentation.
+
+`--max-num-seqs` must also stay under what fits in the KV cache: `Available KV cache
+memory` in the startup log divided by the KV cache of a session. On this card that
+line says 3.4 to 4.2 GiB, so 15 to 19 sessions fit with windows of 1024 and 256.
+Sessions above `--max-num-seqs` wait for a free slot. If more sessions run than fit,
+all of them stall ([#60137](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60137)).
+`Maximum concurrency` in the startup log does not limit sessions: it is the worst
+case for a request of `--max-model-len` tokens with full batches in flight. The
+startup check needs that worst case free, so a large `--max-num-batched-tokens` can
+stop the server from starting.
+
+Each session needs 12.5 tokens/s (`Avg generation throughput` in the log). If the
+GPU does not deliver that, all sessions fall behind real time.

+
+One streaming-input session runs twice on Llama-3.2-1B, every layer overridden to a
+sliding window: with a small max_model_len and the flag on, then with a max_model_len
+that needs no shift. The greedy logprobs must match up to rounding.

+if not current_platform.is_cuda():
+    pytest.skip(reason="Re-anchoring is CUDA only.", allow_module_level=True)
+
+MODEL = "meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct"
+SLIDING_WINDOW = 512
+CHUNK_TOKENS = 120
+NUM_CHUNKS = 40  # 8 to 11 shifts at max_model_len 1536
+# Measured in float32: up to 0.05 with the shifts, up to 2.9 without the rotation.
+LOGPROB_TOLERANCE = 0.2
+
+HF_OVERRIDES = {
+    "layer_types": ["sliding_attention"] * 16,
+    "sliding_window": SLIDING_WINDOW,
+}
+
+
+async def _run_session(
+    gen_tokens: int, **engine_kwargs
+) -> list[tuple[int, dict[int, float]]]:
+    """Returns each generated token with the logprobs of the top tokens."""
+    engine_args = AsyncEngineArgs(
+        model=MODEL,
+        hf_overrides=HF_OVERRIDES,
+        dtype="float32",
+        seed=0,
+        enforce_eager=True,
+        enable_prefix_caching=False,
+        gpu_memory_utilization=0.5,
+        **engine_kwargs,
+    )
+    with set_default_torch_num_threads(1):
+        engine = AsyncLLM.from_engine_args(engine_args)
+
+    rng = random.Random(0)
+    chunks = [
+        [rng.randrange(3, 100000) for _ in range(CHUNK_TOKENS)]
+        for _ in range(NUM_CHUNKS)
+    ]
+
+    async def inputs():
+        for ids in chunks:
+            yield StreamingInput(prompt={"prompt_token_ids": ids})
+
+    params = SamplingParams(
+        max_tokens=gen_tokens,
+        ignore_eos=True,
+        temperature=0.0,
+        logprobs=5,
+        output_kind=RequestOutputKind.DELTA,
+    )
+    outputs: list[tuple[int, dict[int, float]]] = []
+    try:
+        async for out in engine.generate(inputs(), params, "session"):
+            for completion in out.outputs:
+                for token, top in zip(completion.token_ids, completion.logprobs or ()):
+                    assert top is not None
+                    outputs.append(
+                        (token, {tok: lp.logprob for tok, lp in top.items()})
+                    )
+    finally:
+        engine.shutdown()
+    return outputs

+def _spec(rotary_dim: int, base: float, is_neox: bool, scale: int = 1):
+    inv_freq = 1.0 / (
+        base ** (torch.arange(0, rotary_dim, 2, dtype=torch.float32) / rotary_dim)
+    )
+    return RotarySpec(inv_freq.double(), rotary_dim, is_neox, scale)

+def _forward_rotary(x: torch.Tensor, pos: int, spec: RotarySpec) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Rotate ``x`` by +pos, as the forward pass does."""
+    angle = pos * spec.inv_freq
+    rotated = ApplyRotaryEmb.forward_static(
+        x[..., : spec.rotary_dim], angle.cos(), angle.sin(), spec.is_neox
+    )
+    return torch.cat((rotated, x[..., spec.rotary_dim :]), dim=-1)

+    reanchored = apply_inverse_rotary(_forward_rotary(k, p, spec), d, spec)
+    target = _forward_rotary(k, p - d, spec)

+"""Position shifts of streaming sessions for --enable-unbounded-streaming-input."""
+
+from dataclasses import replace

+from vllm.config import SchedulerConfig
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.utils.math_utils import round_down

+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+
+class SessionReanchor:
+    """Keeps streaming sessions under max_model_len by shifting their positions
+    down. The worker re-rotates the cached keys."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        scheduler_config: SchedulerConfig,
+        kv_cache_manager: KVCacheManager,
+        encoder_cache_manager: EncoderCacheManager,
+        max_model_len: int,
+        block_size: int,
+    ) -> None:
+        self.kv_cache_manager = kv_cache_manager
+        self.encoder_cache_manager = encoder_cache_manager
+        self.max_model_len = max_model_len
+        self.block_size = block_size
+
+        windows = []
+        for mgr in kv_cache_manager.coordinator.single_type_managers:
+            # The worker has already checked every KV cache group.
+            assert isinstance(mgr, SlidingWindowManager)
+            windows.append(mgr.sliding_window + mgr.extra_retained_tokens)
+        self.window = max(windows)
+
+        margin = scheduler_config.unbounded_streaming_input_margin_tokens
+        if margin is None:
+            # Half for the tokens generated per input chunk, half between shifts.
+            margin = max((max_model_len - self.window) // 2, 0)
+            minimum = self.window + 2 * block_size - 1
+        else:
+            minimum = self.window + margin + block_size
+        # A shift drops whole blocks, so at least one block must fit between the
+        # window and the trigger.
+        if max_model_len < minimum:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"--enable-unbounded-streaming-input needs max_model_len >= {minimum} "
+                f"(sliding window {self.window}, KV cache block {block_size}), got "
+                f"{max_model_len}."
+            )
+        self.trigger = max_model_len - margin
+
+    def shift(self, request: Request) -> bool:
+        """Shift a session's positions down by d, dropping its d oldest tokens,
+        which are out of the sliding window. Returns False if nothing is dropped."""
+        processed = request.num_computed_tokens
+        has_keys = processed > 0
+        if not has_keys:
+            # Preempted: only the re-prefill from position 0 has to fit.
+            if request.num_tokens < self.max_model_len:
+                return False
+            processed = request.num_tokens - 1
+        # A multiple of the scheduler block size (the LCM of the group block
+        # sizes), so every group drops whole blocks.
+        d = round_down(processed - self.window, self.block_size)
+        if d <= 0:
+            return False
+
+        if has_keys:
+            # A step still in flight after a stop runs at the frontier or past it,
+            # so it only reads what the next step reads.
+            self.kv_cache_manager.remove_skipped_blocks(request.request_id, processed)
+            self.kv_cache_manager.drop_leading_blocks(request.request_id, d)
+            request.num_computed_tokens -= d
+            request.pending_reanchor_d += d
+
+        del request._all_token_ids[:d]
+        # Resuming folded the outputs into the prompt.
+        assert request.prompt_token_ids is not None and not request._output_token_ids
+        del request.prompt_token_ids[:d]
+        request.num_prompt_tokens -= d
+
+        # Drop the mm features that end before d and shift the others.
+        n_drop = 0
+        for mm_feature in request.mm_features:
+            pos = mm_feature.mm_position
+            if pos.offset + pos.length > d:
+                break
+            n_drop += 1
+        if n_drop:
+            self.encoder_cache_manager.drop_leading_inputs(request, n_drop)
+        request.mm_features = [
+            replace(
+                f, mm_position=replace(f.mm_position, offset=f.mm_position.offset - d)
+            )
+            for f in request.mm_features[n_drop:]
+        ]
+
+        logger.info(
+            "Re-anchored %s: positions shifted down by %d.", request.request_id, d
+        )
+        return True

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Key re-rotation for --enable-unbounded-streaming-input.
+
+When the scheduler shifts a session's positions down by d, its cached keys are
+re-rotated by R(-d). RoPE scores only depend on relative positions, so they stay
+the same apart from rounding. Each layer uses its own RoPE, read from the model
+at startup.
+"""
+
+from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from fractions import Fraction
+from typing import Any
+
+import torch
+from torch import nn
+
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.rotary_embedding import (
+    Llama3RotaryEmbedding,
+    RotaryEmbedding,
+    YaRNScalingRotaryEmbedding,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.rotary_embedding.common import ApplyRotaryEmb
+from vllm.utils.torch_utils import async_tensor_h2d
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.utils import NULL_BLOCK_ID
+from vllm.v1.core.sched.output import SchedulerOutput
+from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import (
+    KVCacheConfig,
+    KVCacheGroupSpec,
+    KVQuantMode,
+    SlidingWindowMLASpec,
+    SlidingWindowSpec,
+    UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs,
+)
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class RotarySpec:
+    """How one attention layer rotates its keys."""
+
+    # The layer's float32 frequencies, widened to float64: in float32,
+    # d * inv_freq is off by up to 3e-3 rad at d ~ 1e5.
+    inv_freq: torch.Tensor
+    rotary_dim: int
+    is_neox: bool
+    # Positions this layer advances per scheduled token: 1, or the pool size of a
+    # block-pooled layer (see AttentionSpec.tokens_per_state).
+    position_scale: int
+
+
+# RoPE classes whose angle at position p is p * inv_freq. YaRN scales cos and
+# sin by the same mscale, which leaves the rotation itself unchanged.
+_STATIC_ROPE_INV_FREQ = {
+    RotaryEmbedding: lambda rope: rope._compute_inv_freq(rope.base),
+    Llama3RotaryEmbedding: lambda rope: rope._compute_inv_freq(rope.base),
+    YaRNScalingRotaryEmbedding: lambda rope: rope._compute_inv_freq(
+        rope.scaling_factor
+    ),
+}
+
+
+def collect_rotary_specs(
+    model: nn.Module, position_scales: Mapping[str, int]
+) -> dict[str, RotarySpec]:
+    """Map each attention layer to the RoPE that rotated its cached keys.
+
+    Follows the usual vLLM layout, where the module holding an attention layer
+    (any child with a ``layer_name``) also holds its ``rotary_emb``. Raises if a
+    layer has no RoPE, or one whose angle is not p * inv_freq (M-RoPE, Fourier,
+    long RoPE, ...), or one built for another head size.
+    """
+    owners: dict[str, tuple[Any, nn.Module]] = {}
+    for module in model.modules():
+        rope = getattr(module, "rotary_emb", None)
+        if rope is None:
+            continue
+        for child in module.children():
+            layer_name = getattr(child, "layer_name", None)
+            if layer_name is not None:
+                owners[layer_name] = (rope, child)
+
+    specs: dict[str, RotarySpec] = {}
+    for layer_name, position_scale in position_scales.items():
+        if layer_name not in owners:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "--enable-unbounded-streaming-input: no rotary_emb on the parent "
+                f"module of attention layer {layer_name!r}."
+            )
+        rope, attn = owners[layer_name]
+        get_inv_freq = _STATIC_ROPE_INV_FREQ.get(type(rope))
+        if get_inv_freq is None:
+            supported = ", ".join(cls.__name__ for cls in _STATIC_ROPE_INV_FREQ)
+            raise ValueError(
+                "--enable-unbounded-streaming-input does not support "
+                f"{type(rope).__name__} (layer {layer_name!r}). "
+                f"Supported: {supported}."
+            )
+        # The rotary dims must be the first dims of the key.
+        if rope.head_size != attn.head_size:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"--enable-unbounded-streaming-input: layer {layer_name!r} has head "
+                f"size {attn.head_size}, its RoPE {rope.head_size}."
+            )
+        # On the device of the forward table: pow differs by 1 ulp across devices.
+        with torch.device(rope.cos_sin_cache.device):
+            inv_freq = get_inv_freq(rope).to(torch.float64)
+        specs[layer_name] = RotarySpec(
+            inv_freq=inv_freq,
+            rotary_dim=rope.rotary_dim,
+            is_neox=rope.is_neox_style,
+            position_scale=position_scale,
+        )
+    return specs
+
+
+def init_reanchor_rotary_specs(
+    model: nn.Module,
+    kv_cache_config: KVCacheConfig,
+    forward_context: Mapping[str, Any],
+) -> dict[str, RotarySpec]:
+    """Check that the cached keys of every KV cache layer can be re-rotated in
+    place. Returns the spec of each layer."""
+    position_scales = {}
+    for group in kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups:
+        for layer_name in group.layer_names:
+            spec = group.kv_cache_spec
+            if isinstance(spec, UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs):
+                # KV-sharing aliases have no spec of their own.
+                spec = spec.kv_cache_specs.get(layer_name, spec.first_spec)
+            if not isinstance(spec, SlidingWindowSpec) or isinstance(
+                spec, SlidingWindowMLASpec
+            ):
+                raise ValueError(
+                    "--enable-unbounded-streaming-input needs every attention layer "
+                    f"to use a sliding window; {layer_name!r} uses "
+                    f"{type(spec).__name__}."
+                )
+            layer = forward_context[layer_name]
+            kv = layer.kv_cache
+            position_scale = 1 / Fraction(spec.tokens_per_state)
+            if (
+                spec.kv_quant_mode != KVQuantMode.NONE
+                or spec.num_head_slots is not None
+                or position_scale.denominator != 1
+                or layer.kv_sharing_target_layer_name is not None
+                or kv.dim() != 4
+                or kv.shape[0] != kv_cache_config.num_blocks
+                or kv.shape[-1] != 2 * layer.head_size
+            ):
+                raise ValueError(
+                    "--enable-unbounded-streaming-input needs an unshared, "
+                    "non-quantized KV cache of (blocks, heads, block_size, "
+                    f"2 * head_size); layer {layer_name!r}: "
+                    f"{spec.kv_quant_mode.name}, {tuple(kv.shape)}, "
+                    f"tokens_per_state {spec.tokens_per_state}."
+                )
+            position_scales[layer_name] = int(position_scale)
+    return collect_rotary_specs(model, position_scales)
+
+
+def rerotate_shifted_sessions(
+    scheduler_output: SchedulerOutput,
+    forward_context: Mapping[str, Any],
+    kv_cache_groups: Sequence[KVCacheGroupSpec],
+    specs: Mapping[str, RotarySpec],
+    device: torch.device,
+) -> None:
+    """Re-rotate the cached keys of the sessions the scheduler shifted down in
+    this step. A shifted session is always among the new requests."""
+    reanchor_reqs = scheduler_output.reanchor_reqs
+    assert reanchor_reqs is not None
+    for new_req in scheduler_output.scheduled_new_reqs:
+        d = reanchor_reqs.get(new_req.req_id)
+        if d is not None:
+            group_block_ids = [
+                async_tensor_h2d(
+                    [i for i in ids if i != NULL_BLOCK_ID], device, dtype=torch.long
+                )
+                for ids in new_req.block_ids
+            ]
+            rerotate_cached_keys(
+                forward_context, kv_cache_groups, group_block_ids, d, specs
+            )
+
+
+def rerotate_cached_keys(
+    forward_context: Mapping[str, Any],
+    kv_cache_groups: Sequence[KVCacheGroupSpec],
+    group_block_ids: Sequence[torch.Tensor],
+    d: int,
+    specs: Mapping[str, RotarySpec],
+) -> None:
+    """Apply R(-d) to one request's cached keys in every KV cache group.
+
+    ``group_block_ids[g]`` holds the request's blocks in group ``g``. The blocks
+    allocated for this step hold no live keys yet, so rotating them is fine.
+    """
+    for group, block_ids in zip(kv_cache_groups, group_block_ids, strict=True):
+        for layer_name in group.layer_names:
+            layer = forward_context[layer_name]
+            kv, head_size, spec = layer.kv_cache, layer.head_size, specs[layer_name]
+            # Layer view (blocks, heads, block_size, 2 * head_size): K then V.
+            kv[block_ids, ..., :head_size] = apply_inverse_rotary(
+                kv[block_ids, ..., :head_size], spec.position_scale * d, spec
+            )
+
+
+def apply_inverse_rotary(key: torch.Tensor, d: int, spec: RotarySpec) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Apply R(-d) to ``key`` ([..., head_size], rotary dims first)."""
+    angle = d * spec.inv_freq
+    # In fp32: cos and sin rounded to bf16 would give every key the same error, in
+    # angle and in scale, at each frequency.
+    rotated = ApplyRotaryEmb.forward_static(
+        key[..., : spec.rotary_dim],
+        angle.cos(),
+        -angle.sin(),
+        spec.is_neox,
+        enable_fp32_compute=True,
+    )
+    return torch.cat((rotated, key[..., spec.rotary_dim :]), dim=-1)

Both points from the #45022 review look addressed here — thanks for the thorough follow-up.

`test_voxtral_realtime_reanchor_parity` is exactly the coverage I was after: a real attention forward + re-anchor against a re-anchor-OFF reference asserting token-for-token parity, not just the algebra. Proving the path fired via "a session can't emit more than `max_model_len` output tokens unless its clock was re-anchored down" is a clean way to make it CI-checkable without scraping the subprocess scheduler log.

And the up-front startup validation — rejecting a non-128 decoder `head_dim` and guarding the `pool` derivation so it can't silently fall to 1 — is the right fix for the head_size/`pool` coupling: it fails loud at init instead of silently mis-rotating encoder keys.
